votes.motion: Accept the April 24th minutes as presented

budget_items.topic: Storm water utility fee - town meeting reaction
budget_items.what_was_said: Members discussed resident frustration at town meeting about having to pay the new storm water utility fee, especially those with existing flooding problems. They noted a couple of residents said water leaves their property into the road/system regardless, so they'd still be charged.

The task force discussed the figure presented at town meeting to residents for the residential quarterly fee, and debated whether it was framed as an exact figure or a ceiling under the highest-cost alternative.

budget_items.topic: Total eligible properties for the storm water utility
budget_items.what_was_said: The group reviewed the March document's property count, subtracting properties with no impervious area, water/right-of-way/forested parcels, and municipally owned properties from the total to reach the number eligible for the fee.

budget_items.topic: Budget target and which alternative covers it
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said alternative two, possibly with some cushion for collection shortfalls, was the one that met the storm water program's budget target, citing an expected contribution from Chapter 90 funds.
Members noted this year's Chapter 90 allocation was much higher than usual, cautioning that the higher figure should not be assumed to recur every year.
The group discussed the per-ERU dollar rate under each fee alternative, describing it as a sliding scale between the lowest and highest proposed rates.
Members found what they believed were calculation errors in the tier price table, where dollar amounts did not increase consistently between alternatives across certain tiers.

budget_items.topic: Cost difference for the largest tier between alternatives
budget_items.what_was_said: A member calculated how much more a top-tier property would pay per year moving from the lowest to the second fee alternative.

budget_items.topic: Vacant properties' share of total revenue
budget_items.what_was_said: The task force discussed that vacant-category properties account for a meaningful slice of the projected fee revenue and expressed reluctance to drop that revenue from the consultant's budget.

budget_items.topic: Comparison to Chelmsford's tiered fee structure
budget_items.what_was_said: Members compared Chelmsford's more granular tier system and per-tier dollar rates against Lunenburg's proposed structure, noting Chelmsford charges considerably more at the high end.

budget_items.topic: Comparison to Millis's per-square-foot billing method
budget_items.what_was_said: The group discussed Millis's method of charging a flat unit fee per additional 1,000 square feet of impervious area, and estimated what a large property like Walmart would owe under that method.
A member noted an alternate per-1,000-square-foot rate proposed by the consultant for the lowest alternative, and estimated the resulting bill for a large property.

budget_items.topic: Proposed new tier 11 for largest properties
budget_items.what_was_said: Members agreed informally that properties far above the current top tier's square footage threshold (found via GIS review of large parcels) should have a new, higher tier so they are not charged the same as much smaller top-tier properties.

decisions.decision: A member will write up and send out the outstanding list of questions for the consultant (Nick/Bill) by email so members can review and comment before the next meeting.
The task force will look more closely at Chelmsford's tier structure as a possible model and consider sharing town comparisons with residents.
Leaning toward adding a new top tier (tier 11) above the current largest tier so the biggest properties (over roughly double the current top threshold) pay more than mid-size top-tier properties.
Target the week of June 10-12 for the next meeting and check the consultant's availability for those dates; if unavailable, push the meeting into July.
Informal leaning toward 'alternative two' as the preferred fee structure, but explicitly not a final commitment pending consultant answers.

minutes.headline: Task force debated storm water fee tiers/rates but made no final decision, awaiting consultant's answers
minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force spent most of the meeting scrutinizing the consultant's proposed storm water utility fee tiers, ERU rates, and property classifications (vacant lots, multi-family, and the largest commercial/industrial parcels), finding apparent errors and open questions they could not resolve without the consultant. No fee alternative was formally adopted; the group leaned toward exploring a higher tier for the largest properties and comparing Lunenburg's structure to Chelmsford's, and agreed to compile questions and invite the consultant to the next meeting, tentatively the week of June 10-12.

what_happened.line: The task force reviewed the consultant's proposed storm water fee tiers and rates but made no final decision, citing apparent errors in the tier pricing table.
Members leaned toward a new top tier for the largest properties and toward one fee alternative as preferred, but called both informal pending the consultant's answers.
Open questions remain on how vacant, multi-family and duplex properties would be classified and priced under the fee.
The group agreed to send the consultant a written list of outstanding questions and to compare Lunenburg's proposed tiers against Chelmsford's structure.
The next meeting is tentatively targeted for the week of June 10-12, with the consultant invited, or pushed to July if unavailable.

why_it_matters: Residents already paying the new storm water utility fee could see their tier or rate change depending on which fee alternative and tier structure the task force ultimately recommends.
Owners of vacant, multi-family, duplex or large commercial/industrial parcels have an unresolved classification question that affects what they would be billed.
No fee structure has been adopted yet, so any final proposal will still need to come back to the task force and likely to town meeting.
